newsitem.title: USA: ING Barings sees Argentine stocks up 10-14 pct.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings sees Argentine stocks up 10-14 pct.

text.p: Argentine stocks are likely to rise up to 14 percent in the next 12 months, with the favorite sectors telecommunications, banks and cement, ING Barings analysts said Monday.
In a telephone conference call, they said Buenos Aires' Merval stock exchange would be driven higher largely by greater inflows from local pension funds.

Hernan Ladeuix, head of Argentine research, said pension funds' investments were likely to be between $80 million and $100 million a month in coming months, up from $20 million to $40 million in March and April.

"Bottom line, we are expecting 12-month returns of between 10 to 14 percent for our market, which are modest compared to other countries in the region," he said, noting that the Merval has risen 25 percent so far this year.
"Therefore, in our opinion, stock picking will be very important in our market."
He said Argentina had benefited in part from strong economic growth, steady U.S. interest rates, the influx of pension fund money, and merger-and-acquisition activities, especially involving banks.

The market already had discounted those factors, he said. It now could be affected by mid-term elections in October and by potential economic turmoil in Brazil, one of Argentina's biggest trade partners.
"We continue to be overweight the banks, telcos and cement sectors, which we believe still will be favored by the pickup in the economy," Ladeuix said.
Stock picks included Banco Frances and Banco de Galicia, Telefonica de Argentina and Telecom Argentina and Corporacion Cementera Argentina.
ING Barings also favored oil company YPF SA and CEI Citicorp Holdings SA.
